newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-SEEDS MICKELSON, ELKINGTON BEATEN IN WORLD MATCHPLAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SEEDS MICKELSON, ELKINGTON BEATEN IN WORLD MATCHPLAY.

text.p: American Phil Mickelson and last year's runner-up Steve Elkington, the sixth and eighth seeds, were beaten in the opening round of the World Matchplay championship at Wentworth on Thursday.
Mickelson, the leader of the U.S. money list this year, dropped five of the first seven holes to Vijay Singh of Fiji, recovered to all square after 20 holes but then faded to a one-hole defeat.
He almost forced a playoff. Bunkered beside the green in two at the 36th, Mickelson's sand shot flew into the hole on the fly but bounced out again and finished three feet away.
From off the green, Singh got up and down to win with a four-foot birdie putt.
Australian Elkington, beaten by Ernie Els in last year's final, led by two holes against American Steve Stricker after 18 holes but fell away in the afternoon and went down 3 and 2.

Colin Montgomerie, The European Tour's leading money winner for four successive seasons, beat twice champion Ian Woosnam 3 and 2 in their all-British battle, while American seventh seed Mark O'Meara crushed Japan's Nobuo Serizawa 7 and 5 in the other match.

The top four seeds had byes. Top seed Els will face Stricker in Friday's second round, British Open champion Tom Lehman faces O'Meara, U.S. Open champion Steve Jones takes on Singh and PGA winner Mark Brooks meets Montgomerie.
